note: The measurement roadmap: indicators this platform argues should exist but for which no observation is yet available. They are deliberately NOT part of methodology v1.3 and do not enter any score, declaring a gap is not the same as filling it. Promote one by moving its definition into indicators.json and supplying an observation.

items.name: Accelerated compute available to researchers
items.rationale: The actual currency of AI work; headline FLOPs say nothing about access.

items.name: Cost per GPU-hour, domestic versus regional
items.rationale: Determines whether training locally is rational at all.

items.name: National compute utilisation
items.rationale: Idle capacity is a different policy problem from absent capacity.

items.name: Data centre power usage effectiveness
items.rationale: Energy efficiency of the hosting estate.

items.name: AI workload share of national electricity demand
items.rationale: Directly tests the claim that one campus would draw a third of generation.

items.name: Renewable share powering data centres
items.rationale: Rwanda's largely hydro grid is an unmeasured comparative advantage.

items.name: Water withdrawal for data-centre cooling
items.rationale: Cooling competes with agriculture in a water-constrained highland economy.

items.name: Pilot survival rate at 24 months
items.rationale: The 2026 review states outright that this is unmeasured; it is the single most diagnostic adoption metric.

items.name: Time from pilot to production
items.rationale: Distinguishes an ecosystem that ships from one that pilots.

items.name: Citizens served by AI-supported public services
items.rationale: Converts deployment counts into reach.

items.name: Transactions processed with AI in the loop
items.rationale: The denominator for any productivity claim.

items.name: Public services with an AI component
items.rationale: Comparable across countries via e-government service catalogues.

items.name: Agencies publishing an AI system inventory
items.rationale: Prerequisite for the transparency register the 2026 review calls for.

items.name: Decommissioned or abandoned AI systems
items.rationale: Nobody publishes failures. A platform that did would be genuinely distinctive.

items.name: Public AI systems running on domestically-owned models
items.rationale: Measures the layer of the stack Rwanda actually controls.

items.name: AI contracts carrying a model-ownership clause
items.rationale: The cheapest governance gap identified in 2026, and the most valuable.

items.name: Public data processed in-country
items.rationale: Tests the data localisation regime in practice rather than in law.

items.name: Kinyarwanda tokens in openly licensed corpora
items.rationale: Free, versioned and queryable; directly measures the sovereign layer.

items.name: Openly licensed Rwandan models published
items.rationale: Automatable daily.

items.name: Downloads of Rwandan open models
items.rationale: Demand signal for the sovereign language layer.

items.name: Kinyarwanda speech recognition word error rate
items.rationale: Quality, not just existence, of the language capability.

items.name: Government AI spend awarded to domestic vendors
items.rationale: Procurement is the state's most powerful available instrument.

items.name: Algorithmic impact assessments completed
items.rationale: The data protection law already requires them for high-risk processing.

items.name: High-risk systems with documented human oversight
items.rationale: Oversight claimed is not oversight evidenced.

items.name: Independent model evaluations conducted
items.rationale: A testbed must be able to certify what it tested.

items.name: AI incidents recorded and resolved
items.rationale: No incident register exists anywhere in the framework.

items.name: Redress requests concerning automated decisions
items.rationale: Rights without a measured remedy are rights on paper.

items.name: Breach notifications within the 48-hour statutory clock
items.rationale: Tests whether the enforceable regime is actually enforced.

items.name: Public trust in government use of AI
items.rationale: Adoption without consent is fragile.

items.name: Data-labelling workforce covered by labour protections
items.rationale: The continental index flags this as a blind spot no national strategy addresses.

items.name: Gender gap in AI and digital skills participation
items.rationale: Nothing on the platform is currently disaggregated.

items.name: Gender gap in measured AI usage
items.rationale: For a country at 0.20x expected usage, distribution is the policy question.

items.name: Rural–urban smartphone ownership gap
items.rationale: Device access is the binding demand-side constraint.

items.name: Entry smartphone cost as a share of monthly median income
items.rationale: Handsets average USD 160 against the incomes that must buy them.

items.name: 1 GB mobile data as a share of monthly median income
items.rationale: The international affordability target is 2%.

items.name: Public AI services available in Kinyarwanda
items.rationale: Language access is the difference between a service existing and being usable.

items.name: Digital accessibility compliance of public services
items.rationale: Disability access is absent from the framework entirely.

items.name: Measured AI contribution to GDP
items.rationale: NST2 carries a 5–6% target with no measurement behind it.

items.name: Value realised against the 2022 sizing, by sector
items.rationale: Closes the loop on the 589m potential the platform already publishes.

items.name: AI-related job postings
items.rationale: Leading indicator of demand, available before employment statistics.

items.name: Wage premium for AI skills
items.rationale: Whether the skills programme pays for its participants.

items.name: Net migration of AI and technical talent
items.rationale: The 2026 review names retention as a critical risk with no strategy behind it.

items.name: Firms reporting productivity gains from AI
items.rationale: The micro evidence behind any macro claim.

items.name: AI venture funding per capita
items.rationale: Comparable across the peer set.

items.name: Follow-on funding rate for AI start-ups
items.rationale: Distinguishes a pipeline from a cohort.

items.name: AI service exports
items.rationale: Tests the business-process repositioning the 2026 agenda proposes.

proposedComposites.name: Conversion Efficiency
proposedComposites.question: Is capability turning into deployment? Currently visible only as a raw gap.

proposedComposites.name: Sovereignty Index
proposedComposites.construction: model ownership + local hosting + local language capability + domestic vendor share
proposedComposites.question: How much of the stack does Rwanda control?

proposedComposites.name: Assurance Index
proposedComposites.construction: evaluation capability + oversight coverage + incident handling + redress
proposedComposites.question: Can Rwanda certify what it deploys?

proposedComposites.name: Inclusion Index
proposedComposites.construction: gender, rural–urban, affordability and language access
proposedComposites.question: Who is excluded from the 0.20x usage figure?

proposedComposites.name: Compute Adequacy
proposedComposites.construction: available capacity ÷ estimated demand, bounded by the energy envelope
proposedComposites.question: Can Rwanda physically run what it plans?
